title: Signalboard: customer asks -> sprint buckets (June 2026)
content:
Purpose:
A lightweight, action-oriented signalboard that converts recent customer feedback (May-Jun 2026) into concrete sprint-sized proposals. The goal: stop re-highlighting the same asks in weekly calls, and get a set of validated quick wins and scoped bets into eng/product backlog by next planning.

Context and constraints:
- Source: 18 post-demo notes, 27 CS calls, 6 enterprise onboarding retros, and support tickets flagged as "Ask: product change" between 2026-05-20 and 2026-06-12.
- Customers: mix of mid-market SaaS and two regulated enterprise pilots (healthcare, finance).
- Risk tolerance: quick wins should be reversible; bigger bets need SLO/infra review.

Top signals (one-line):
1) Default model fallback behavior is creating noisy cost overruns for bursty workloads.
   - Quote: "We had cost spikes when the primary model OOM'd; no obvious fallback policy."
2) Embedding latency variability on small batches (<=8) degrades pipelined product demos.
   - Quote: "Embedding feels fine in bulk, but demos stutter and make us look unreliable."
3) Token-level billing transparency request: customers want route-by-route token cost breakdowns.
   - Quote: "We need to show product managers which routes cost the most."
4) API error messages are too opaque for retry logic (need machine-readable error categories).
5) Private (VPC) deploys: install checklist gaps around KMS integrations and audit-log verification.
6) Console: rollout metrics per model version (A/B style) are requested by platform teams.

Signal prioritization (impact x effort quick scan):
- Quick wins (<=2w dev + 1 QA):
  QW1: Add explicit fallback policy toggle in API (policy: fallback-to-smaller-model OR queued retry).
    - Proposed owner: product-hosted-api (Linnea) + eng-serving-runtime.
    - Rough effort: 1 sprint for API flag + runtime routing hook.
    - Impact: high for enterprises running mixed loads; reduces cost/regression risk.
    - Example ticket: JIRA-CS-3421 (linked).

  QW2: Add extra debug fields to embedding response headers: backend_model, request_batched, queue_time_ms.
    - Owner: developer-experience + observability.
    - Effort: ~3 days to add headers + docs.
    - Impact: immediate relief for demo flakiness triage.

- Small bets (2–6w):
  SB1: Route-level token cost breakdown in Console + export CSV.
    - Owner: product-console + billing.
    - Effort: 3–4 weeks (UI, backend aggregation, permissioning).
    - Impact: medium-high for customers trying to manage spend; sales enablement win.
    - Data ask: need sample access patterns from finance customers to ensure aggregation granularity is useful.

  SB2: Machine-readable API error taxonomy and HTTP subcodes (retriable, auth, quota, model-fallback).
    - Owner: eng-serving-runtime + API.
    - Effort: 2 sprints with stable test harness.
    - Impact: reduces support load and enables client-side resilient logic.

- Platform / strategic (6+ w):
  PL1: Model fallback orchestration: automated graceful degradation across region/capacity/model-variant when OOM/latency spike occurs.
    - Owner: serving-runtime + platform-engineering.
    - Effort: multi-sprint; requires simulation infra and fallbacks policy UI.
    - Impact: very high for reliability SLAs; high engineering cost.

  PL2: Private deploy audit checklist & KMS validation flows (packaged installer + docs).
    - Owner: private-deployments + security-and-compliance.
    - Effort: ~6–8 weeks with legal/security signoffs.
    - Impact: removes largest blocker for 2 regulated pilots.

Customer quotes (representative):
- "We need to be able to say exactly which route burned tokens for our CFO – otherwise we can't justify scale." (SaaS analytics, Series B)
- "When one model fails, our product times out and we lose users. We need a cleaner fallback that's not manual." (marketplace platform)
- "Embedding jitter during demos loses trust. If you add simple headers or a flag, that's enough for us to proceed." (enterprise trial)

Unresolved questions / assumptions to validate quickly:
- How often do customers prefer cheaper-but-slower fallback vs always-prefer-latency for a route? (Need route-level telemetry)
- Are token-cost exports subject to PII concerns across EU customers? (ask security & legal)
- Priority between console-level cost export vs API-level header debug – which one unlocks most deals this quarter?

Immediate next steps (this week):
1) Run a 30-minute alignment with product-hosted-api, serving-runtime, and console on Monday. Agenda: signal readout + pick QW1 owner. (Owner: Aisha)
2) Create two spike PRs:
   - Spike A: Add embedding response headers for queue_time_ms and backend_model (owner: Marco).
   - Spike B: Add API error subcode enum in SDK responses (owner: Connor).
3) Draft a 1-pager for sales with the planned quick wins and expected ship dates (owner: Linnea).

Proposed acceptance criteria (for quick wins):
- Fallback toggle: can be toggled in API request param; fallback model is chosen from the model catalog variants; integration test for a simulated OOM returns fallback within SLO.
- Embedding headers: presence of headers in 99% of small-batch requests in staging; docs updated.
- Error taxonomy: SDK surfaces subcode field usable for retry logic; at least 2 major clients adopt in canary.

Notes to self / workshop fragments:
- Possible UX for fallback toggle: request param + profile in Console (per-route default).
- Consider opt-in pilot for regulated customers to test fallback behavior in Private deployment.
- Ticketing: create JIRA epic CS-SIGNALBOARD-06-2026 and child tasks per bucket.

Attachments / references:
- Link to raw notes folder: CONFLUENCE-Redwood-CS-Signals-2026 (contains call snippets and full quotes).
- Related support tickets summarized in spreadsheet: slack:/files/embedding-latency-spreadsheet-2026-06.csv

Bottom line:
We have multiple high-leverage quick fixes (headers, error taxonomy, simple fallback toggle) that are low effort and unblock demos/sales and reduce support load. Recommend we push QW1 and QW2 into the next sprint, kick off the small-bet work concurrently as scoped spikes, and begin scoping the platform projects for Q3 planning.

-- End of note (work-in-progress)
